newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Bell Telecom seen stirring Manila's telecom set-up.
newsitem.headline: Bell Telecom seen stirring Manila's telecom set-up.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court's decision this week paving the way for local firm Bell Telecom to obtain license as a nationwide phone provider has annoyed other firms and analysts said it could upset the whole system.

"The court's decision gives Bell Telecom the right to be heard but it would upset the scheme of things. It puts the wisdom of the service area scheme into question," Johnson Chua, economist at the University of Asia and the Pacific, said on Wednesday.
"If Bell Telecom is given a nationwide permit, then its going to set a precedent for other telecom firms to ask for the same," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital Inc.
Under the law, the Philippines has already been divided into 11 service areas.

"Our position is out of fairness and common sense. Bell Telecom must first prove that it can install the phones on a limited area just like everybody else," Bayan Telecommunications Holdings (BayanTel) executive vice-president Primitivo Penaranda told Reuters.
BayanTel is the telecommunications arm of Benpres Holdings Corp.
Penaranda said BayanTel should have the first crack at a nationwide licence since it was ahead of Bell Telecom in seeking such a permit.
He said that of all the firms under the service area scheme, BayanTel had completed installation of 350,000 lines in a year and a half, ahead of the three year required period.
Analysts predicted it would not be smooth sailing for Bell Telecom as it faced stiff opposition from companies that are part of the service area scheme.

"It's going to be a long legal debacle. Other operators will likely pursue legal issues and they will be tied up with this battle and Bell Telecom will not be able to pursue its goals," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities Phils.

Bell Telecommunications Philippines, owned by a group of local investors, had applied in 1993 for a permit to operate nationwide phone services and it was approved by two of three commissioners of the National Telecommunications Commission.
But since the dissenting vote came from the head of the Commission Simeon Kintanar, the application was turned down.
On Monday, the Supreme Court upheld Bell Telecom's contention that the Commission was a collegial body and that the decision of the majority should been upheld.

"We are very happy, the decision is very timely in the light of the failure of the service area scheme. It now gives the NTC the chance to remedy the flaws and defects of the scheme," Rogelio Quevedo, legal counsel of Bell Telecom told Reuters.
"The three year period for service areas assignees is coming to an end but where are the phones?," asked Quevedo.
Officials of the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, which is at present the sole operator of nationwide services, did not want to comment on the issue.
Bell Telecom's has made ambitious projections, saying it could corner 25 percent of the market in its first year.
But analysts doubted it. "PLDT is losing market share but Bell Telecom cannot get a piece of the pie overnight but perhaps over time," said Liboro.
"It's a Pyrrhic victory for Bell Telecom. They may have won the first battle but not the war, not yet" said Guoco's Mejia. Conversion $ = 26.3 pesos
